title: R' Yehuda bar Menashya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R' Yehudah bar Menashya. A precious homily of his has been preserved for us in the Babylonian Talmud, at Megillah 14a. He expounded the verse "for there is none beside You" (ki ein bilteikha): Do not read bilteikha but levalotekha, “[there is none] to outlast You” — unlike the way of the Holy One, blessed be He, the way of flesh and blood: the works of a man's hands wear him out, whereas the Holy One, blessed be He, wears out the works of His hands. And "there is no rock like our God" (ein tzur) — there is no artist (tzayyar) like our God: the Holy One, blessed be He, fashioned a form within a form, etc. And at Berakhot 10a

the reading, Hyman reports, is R' Yehudah bar Menakhya, but in Dikdukei Soferim the reading is as in Megillah. And in the Jerusalem Talmud, Kilayim ch. 1, halakhah 2: R' Yudan bar Menashe said: A person takes one seed from inside a cucumber and plants it, etc. And at the beginning of Taanit ch. 2 there is a dispute between R' Yudan son of R' Menashe and Rashbag as to why they place ashes of burnt matter upon the ark. And this name is likewise mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 32 (section 4), Midrash Tehillim 1:3,

and Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 31. And it appears to Hyman that he is R' Yehudah bar Menashya. And in the Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat ch. 6, beginning of halakhah 5, it states: Anan (or R' Aun) bar Immi said before Rabbi Yehudah Menashya bar Menashe Yirmeyah. Hyman adds: Possibly it should read R' Yehudah bar Menashyah, and the scribe wrote two readings, bar Menashya or bar Menashe, and afterwards they dropped the word bar.

notes.text: Penei Moshe explains meah in the named Kilayim1:2 paragraph as a seed from inside the fruit, not a coin’s worth. The biological claim is translated as the cited teaching, not modern botanical advice. The garbled final Shabbat chain and Hyman’s two-reading conjecture remain a source question.

Two whole saved scalars were read and checked against raw SHA256, selector and actual edition metadata: Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat chapter6, text index4/subindex1 (499 characters), and Zhytomyr1862 Ohr Zarua II84:1 (7749 characters). The first preserves Anan כר׳ Immi saying before Rabbi Yehudah Menashyaya bar Menashe Yirmeyah. The supplied Anan (or R' Aun) BAR Immi remains beside that digital כר׳ form, without replacing either reading or resolving its syntax. The local full Rabbi before Yehudah is explicit in this Shabbat scalar only; it supplies no full title for the notice heading, the homily speaker, the Berakhot name, the Kilayim/Taanit speakers, or Hyman's proposed identity. The selected Ohr Zarua medieval quotation instead reads Chanan bar Imi said before full Rav Yehudah IN THE NAME OF Menashe bar Yirmeyah. In that quotation Yehudah is the addressee and Menashe bar Yirmeyah the reported transmitter. It is a digital medieval quotation, not an observed manuscript or printed-page collation; it neither adopts Hyman's specific Yehudah bar Menashya identification nor proves his two-reading/lost-bar scribal history. Anan/Aun/Chanan, Immi/Imi, Menashya/Menashyaya/Menashe/Menashyah and Yehuda/Yehudah forms remain distinct without name harmonization, authority merger, new genealogy or chronology. The supplied full garbled sequence retains its ambiguous parsing. Hyman's IT APPEARS and POSSIBLY SHOULD READ remain expressly tentative and attributed; his report of TWO readings, bar Menashya OR bar Menashe, and AFTERWARDS THEY omitted the WORD BAR remains inside that conjecture, with the agents unresolved. The source final מנשיה is distinguished as Menashyah from earlier מנשיא Menashya, not silently harmonized. Earlier full Rabbi/Rabban expansions are archived exactly; unsupported abbreviated titles now remain R', and Rashbag remains unexpanded rather than a freshly admitted Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. The older Penei Moshe seed explanation, current one-seed/from-inside wording and earlier coin-worth/pitma wording remain historical reviewed context, not fresh whole Kilayim/commentary verification or botanical advice. No new whole Megillah, Berakhot, Taanit, Bereshit Rabbah, Midrash Tehillim, Pesikta or Dikdukei Soferim text was read this wake; the supplied homily and all those locator readings remain source reports. The source PRECIOUS homily/PRESERVED FOR US, DO NOT READ X BUT Y, NOT like flesh and blood, wear-him-out versus God-wears-out-His-works contrast, NO rock/NO artist wordplay and FORM WITHIN FORM remain, with the inherited contextual bracket [there is none] disclosed and the old to-wear-You-out rendering archived. The quoted biblical fragments and etc remain incomplete rather than expanded from another text. The seed teaching keeps ONE and plants-it/etc, and the source dispute asks WHY they place burnt ashes UPON THE ARK; no answer is supplied. Menakhya versus Menashya, Yudan BAR Menashe versus BI R' Menashe and the source father/son direction remain without identity admission. Dikdukei Soferim's reported AS IN Megillah is Hyman's uncollated apparatus claim. Midrash Tehillim1:3 remains beside the old81:3 history; Pesikta31 is unsided, not an invented31a, and BR32section4/BEGINNINGTaanit2/BEGINNINGShabbat6hal5 remain conventional contextual locators without new printed mapping. The whole printed notice is in volume II, p. 564. The consulted Megillah 14a Hebrew names Rav Yehuda bar Menashya; Berakhot 10a names Rabbi Yehuda bar Menasya, beside Hyman’s Menakhya and his reported Dikdukei Soferim reading. These occurrences do not establish a global title or identity, and the exact apparatus remains uncollated. Both whole passages support the outlasting contrast and the artist wordplay; their fuller explanations are not inserted into Hyman’s abridgement. The whole consulted Penei Moshe on Kilayim 1:2 explains meah as a seed inside the fruit. Guggenheimer’s English describes a small piece of pericarp, including seed and surrounding tissue. These are textual interpretations, not modern botanical advice. The whole Guggenheimer Shabbat 6:5 passage has Anan כר׳ Immi and the difficult Yehudah/Menashyaya/Menashe/Yirmeyah sequence. The whole medieval Ohr Zarua II 84:1 quotation instead has Chanan bar Imi speaking before Rav Yehudah in the name of Menashe bar Yirmeyah. That is a different parsing, not proof of Hyman’s proposed Yehudah bar Menashya or his two-reading and lost-bar conjecture. His “it appears” and “possibly” remain tentative, with the agents of the alleged omission unresolved. The exact Taanit, Bereshit Rabbah, Midrash Tehillim, Pesikta and Dikdukei Soferim printings remain uncollated here. All existing notes are preserved verbatim.
